title: CyberDualEval: Measuring Dual-Use Cyber Risks in Frontier Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.30533v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: While frontier language models are becoming capable cybersecurity assistants, they also create a dual-use cyber risk: the same capabilities that help defenders identify and analyze vulnerabilities can similarly help attackers weaponize them. Existing cyber benchmarks measure either raw offensive capability or generic refusal behavior, overlooking the dual-use cyber assessment of preserving benign security utility while refusing assistance that materially advances misuse. We introduce CyberDualEval, a benchmark with 430 vulnerable tasks for measuring dual-use cyber risk in frontier language models. Each task is decomposed into three phases of increasing operationalization: security analysis, proof-of-concept generation, and exploit generation. To quantify the residual cyber risk, we annotate each task with a Task Weaponization Score that measures how much work remains to turn the resulting artifact into unauthorized cyber misuse. CyberD

translated_title: CyberDualEval：衡量前沿语言模型的两用网络风险
translated_abstract: 随着前沿语言模型逐渐成为能力强大的网络安全助手，它们也带来了两用网络风险：帮助防御者识别和分析漏洞的相同能力，同样可以帮助攻击者将漏洞武器化。现有的网络基准要么衡量原始的攻击能力，要么衡量泛化的拒绝行为，忽视了两用网络评估——即在保持良性安全实用性的同时，拒绝那些实质性推进滥用的协助。我们提出了 CyberDualEval，一个包含430个漏洞任务、用于衡量前沿语言模型两用网络风险的基准。每个任务被分解为操作性逐步增强的三个阶段：安全分析、概念验证（PoC）生成和漏洞利用生成。为了量化残余网络风险，我们为每个任务标注了任务武器化分数（Task Weaponization Score），用于衡量将模型生成的产物转化为未经授权的网络滥用还需要多少额外工作。
tldr: 提出了CyberDualEval基准，通过430个分三阶段递进（安全分析、概念验证生成、漏洞利用生成）的漏洞任务以及衡量残余风险的任务武器化分数，评估前沿语言模型能否在保留良性安全能力的同时拒绝实质性助推网络滥用。
en_tdlr: CyberDualEval is a benchmark with 430 vulnerable tasks across three increasingly operationalized phases (security analysis, PoC generation, exploit generation) and a Task Weaponization Score to quantify residual risk, measuring whether frontier language models preserve benign security utility while refusing assistance that materially advances cyber misuse.
